summary: Build practical mini-grid planning, sizing, tariff, and feasibility skills in 5 days. Enroll for expert-led rural electrification training.
lede: Mini-grid and rural electrification training helps you assess electricity demand, screen sites, select suitable system architectures, and size hybrid systems for decentralized power projects. You will develop practical skills in load forecasting, tariff design, financial viability assessment, and operational planning. The course guides you through creating a load profile, site assessment matrix, and mini-grid business case for project decision-makers. It also introduces remote monitoring, digital asset management, productive-use integration, and community governance while addressing incomplete data, financing constraints, technical risks, and stakeholder alignment.
audienceIntro: This mini-grid and rural electrification training is designed for professionals who plan, design, finance, regulate, or manage decentralized energy access projects and need practical outputs they can use immediately.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of electricity fundamentals, basic project development concepts, and spreadsheet-based analysis. Prior exposure to solar PV, distribution systems, or energy access projects is helpful, but not mandatory. A laptop with spreadsheet software is required for feasibility exercises, and familiarity with financial calculation in Excel or equivalent tools will improve the hands-on portions. Coding is not required. Advanced concepts are taught at operational level for planning and decision support, not at engineering-commissioning depth.
